brief: A habit tracker as a garden — daily completion waters plants, streaks bloom, neglect wilts

dominant_strengths: Strong central metaphor: plants visibly bloom or wilt under their habit cards, creating emotional stakes and instant legibility of state
Charming sky-to-soil scene grounds the system spatially — sun, clouds, and earth give the metaphor a coherent world
Distinct visual states (bloomed flower, sprout, wilted stem) communicate streak health without needing numbers
dominant_weaknesses: Severe overlap between Garden Stats panel and the right two habit cards breaks layout integrity and signals broken responsive logic
Card typography is generic and inconsistent — 'days' label sizing competes with the streak number, weakening hierarchy
Cloud shapes collide with the title and stats panel obscures content; z-index and spacing feel unresolved rather than intentional
fix_priorities: Resolve the stats panel collision — dock it as a sidebar or collapsible card so habits remain fully visible
Establish a consistent card grid with breathing room; align flower bases to a true ground line
Refine typography scale: bold streak count, muted unit label, and a single accent weight for habit names
Differentiate plant growth stages more dramatically (seedling → bud → bloom → wilt) to amplify the metaphor
rationale.norman_balance: Visceral metaphor charm leads, reflective meaning (watching your garden) is strong, but behavioral clarity suffers from layout collisions and weak hierarchy.
rationale.intent_fit: The garden metaphor is executed conceptually well — watering, blooming, and wilting all map cleanly to habit states — but execution flaws undermine daily usability.
